content.comment_body: Hello everyone, I'm new to [product_name] and this is my first post. I have a project where the timers need to be adjustable by the end users, but I can't figure out how to do this. While I managed to set up message text and assign buttons to a counter, I don't know how to let users change timer values directly. Any help is appreciated. [user_name]
Hello [user_name], try searching for "timer key [product_name]" or similar to find relevant answers. Best regards, [user_name]

Hi [user_name], 1) Timer parameters can be modified only through the [product_name] parameter settings menu (Set param). 2) All program blocks are labeled with IDs like Bxxx. 3) Identify the required blocks by their numbers and, if needed, assign short names. Protect all other blocks except the timer blocks in the block's properties. 4) After loading the program into [product_name], only unprotected blocks appear in the parameter settings (Set param).

That's not entirely accurate; you can use counter values, analog inputs, etc. to assign the timer value. In the timer's properties window, there's a button labeled Reference for this purpose. See the attachment for an example.

analysis.insight_summary: The user was initially unsure how to allow end users to adjust timer values directly with device keys. The responses clarified that timer parameters can typically be changed in the parameter menu, and it's possible to use counter or analog values via the 'Reference' button in the timer properties. This discussion corrected initial misunderstandings and outlined configuration possibilities.
analysis.user_expectations: The user wants end users to be able to modify timer values easily and intuitively via keys or an accessible interface, rather than relying only on system parameter menus.
